review.method: acceptance suite run locally with the retail capability; this harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR and a second production re-measurement of the cinematic trigger inventory through the production container discovery (ZBD/zrdr.zbd member fmv.zrd) and the production ROF tree reader (GOSDATA/ASSETS/crimson.rof members ASSETS/LAYOUT.CSV and the CAMPAIGNINTRO/FINALCINEMA/PASSENGERCABIN/CTL script members), rustc and Cargo.lock; validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass. The consumer trace is cs_content::cinematics::measure_retail_cinematics, and the hashed cinematic-inventory.json artifact records each source member's decoded sha256, every video's measured triggers and Resolved fields with their claim ids, and every fragment's occurrence count and first offset, so a reviewer can re-derive every claim from the artifact alone. The inventory names exactly the ten retail videos: MSopen1 and zipper from the INTRO FMV sequence, Chap0 from the CHAP0 sequence, CrimFlag from five layout movie records (one superseded by the constructed chapter name), Final from the final-cinema record, and chap1 through chap5 from the measured chapter construction. Skippability is Known(true) only where a page's own skip handlers and done handler measured it (the chapter intro and the final cinema); pause policy and master clock are explicit unknowns everywhere, the .mpg label is the original's own extension, and no declared-vocabulary semantic action is stated by any named source. LIMITATION: Which engine event invokes the INTRO and CHAP0 FMV sequences — and so when msopen1.mpg, zipper.mpg and chap0.mpg play — was not read: the decrypted engine image registers both sequence names against fmv.zrd at startup, but the invocation sites were not followed, and no named script source handles these sequences. Affected content: msopen1.mpg, zipper.mpg, chap0.mpg, whose skippability and semantic end are explicit unknowns for the same reason. Resolving evidence: an executable-analysis stage over the engine image, or an original-run capture. LIMITATION: The value domains of native callbacks 2151 (the chapter movie's FC / nmissid) and 3104 (the final-cinema gate) are engine state no installation byte states, so which chapter number each chap<N>.mpg belongs to, and when the final cinema is gated off, stay unread — exactly the F14-D chapter-binding unknown, now with the 3104 gate added. Affected content: chap1.mpg through chap5.mpg and final.mpg. Resolving evidence: an original-run capture of the callbacks' returns (human/original-run only) or a verified executable-analysis stage. LIMITATION: The simulation-pause policy and master clock of every retail scene are explicit unknowns (claims f40.d2.retail.pause.unmeasured and f40.d2.retail.clock.unmeasured): the named sources run in the UI shell and no byte read here states the engine player's behavior; the framerate settings the movie control sends around play/loop/stop are interface frame-rate measures, not a pause statement. Affected content: all ten videos. Resolving task: F40-B/F40-C (the media player consumer) or an original-run capture. LIMITATION: No codec, duration or frame size is claimed for any video: the streams are not decoded, and the measured label is the original's own .mpg extension (claim f40.d2.retail.format.mpg), not a codec identity. Affected content: all ten videos. Resolving task: F40-B's decoder stage. LIMITATION: Retail is read access to the installation's own files, not an original run: the inventory verifies that the named sources state each trigger, never that the original plays a given file for a given player action. Affected content: every fidelity claim about the ten videos. Resolving evidence: an original-run capture. LIMITATION: The teardown path is unread: the pages send no 11000 stop to the movie control when they skip or end (the measured FINALCINEMA and CAMPAIGNINTRO done handlers run only script_run/script_continue/script_end plus a mail to the ambient page), so how the engine stops a movie handle whose owning page ended is engine-side state no named source states. Affected content: the skip paths of chap1.mpg through chap5.mpg and final.mpg, and any claim that skipping cleanly stops playback. Resolving task: F40-D4's executable analysis, or an original-run capture.
